title: Traditional Chinese Medicine for Helicobacter Pylori Infection: Evidence Assessment
author: Xiao-bei Si
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xthfnj6

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Conduct a systemic literature search across specified databases and sources up to December 16th, 2018.

substeps.instruction: Search the following databases: MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure Database (CNKI), Chinese VIP Information (VIP), Chinese Medical Databases (CMB), and Wan-Fang Database.
Include academic journals, dissertations, and conference proceedings regardless of gray literature status.

Utilize the Medline search strategy: (#1 'Helicobacter pylori'[Mesh] OR Helicobacter pylori[Title/Abstract]) AND (#2 'Medicine, Chinese Traditional'[Mesh] OR herbal medicine[Title/Abstract] OR Chinese medicine[Title/Abstract] OR #3 'Berberine'[Mesh] OR 'Berberine Alkaloids'[Mesh] OR allicin[Title/Abstract] OR garlicin[Title/Abstract] OR Qi Zhi Wei Tong[Title/Abstract] OR Wen Wei Shu[Title/Abstract] OR Jing Hua Wei Kang[Title/Abstract] OR Ban Xia Xie Xin[Title/Abstract]) AND (#5 'meta-analysis'[Publication Type] OR meta analysis[Title/Abstract] OR meta-analysis[Title/Abstract] OR systemic review[Title/Abstract]).
Search the reference lists of identified studies for additional relevant titles.

steps.title: Screen Literature Based on Criteria
steps.instruction: Filter retrieved trials using specific inclusion and exclusion criteria through a two-step independent review process.

substeps.instruction: Apply Inclusion Criteria: (1) Patients: Hp infectors (diagnosed per 'Fifth Chinese National Consensus Report on the management of Helicobacter pylori infection'); (2) Interventions: Chinese medicine (herbs, proprietary medicine, or extractives) with or without western therapy; (3) Control: Western medicine only; (4) Outcomes: Main outcome is eradication rate; secondary outcomes include side effect rate, remission rate of digestive symptoms, and ulcer healing rate; (5) Study type: Systemic review and/or meta-analyses (SR/MA).

Apply Exclusion Criteria: (1) Redundant publications; (2) Studies titled 'meta-analysis' or 'systemic review' that do not perform meta-synthesis calculations; (3) In vitro systemic reviews; (4) Abstracts or protocols.
Step 1: Two reviewers independently screen titles and abstracts.
Step 2: Two reviewers independently screen full texts for final assessment.
Resolve any disagreements through discussion or consultation with another specialist.

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Two reviewers independently extract data from the included SR/MAs using piloted forms.

substeps.instruction: Extract the following items: authors, publication year, sample size, intervention groups, main outcome (eradication rate), and secondary outcomes (remission of digestive symptoms, healing of digestive ulcers, and side effects).
Define eradication rate as the negative rate after eradication therapy.
Define ulcer healing based on endoscopy: 'Curing' (disappearance of lesion/inflammation), 'Effectiveness' (lesion narrowed < 50%), and 'Non-effectiveness' (narrowed but > 50%).
Calculate Healing rate as (curing number / total number × 100%).
Calculate Total effectiveness rate as [(total number – non-effectiveness number) / total number × 100%].
Define total remission rate of digestive symptoms as the percentage of patients with relief of any digestive symptoms.
Define side effect rate as the percentage of patients with at least one side effect.

steps.title: Assess Methodological Quality
steps.instruction: Two reviewers independently assess the quality of each included review using the AMSTAR scale.

substeps.instruction: Use a piloted form to evaluate 11 AMSTAR items, including: a priori design, duplicate study selection/data extraction, comprehensive search, gray literature status, list of included/excluded studies, characteristics of included studies, assessment of scientific quality of included studies, use of quality in conclusions, appropriateness of methods to combine findings, publication bias assessment, and conflict of interest statement.
Score each item: 'yes' = 1 point; 'no', 'cannot answer', or 'not applicable' = 0 points.
Calculate the total score for each SR/MA.

steps.title: Assess Reporting Characteristics
steps.instruction: Evaluate the reporting quality of included SR/MAs using the PRISMA statement.

substeps.instruction: Grade each of the 27 PRISMA items as 'adequately reported', 'not reported', or 'partially reported'.
For 'Protocol and registration': Grade as 'adequately reported' if both protocol and registration (with number/info) are stated; 'partially reported' if only one is stated.
For 'data item': Grade as 'adequately reported' if both data item and definition are stated; 'partially reported' if only data items are stated.
